findings.text: No test for new behavior (acceptance 6). git diff ccd183c 1119b04 -- test is 0 lines; grep -rl 'lastActiveAt|faded|Archive (' test returns nothing. Untested: listActors lastActiveAt = max(message, session heartbeat, created_at) incl. the created_at floor; the avatar-in-cache fix (dane.js:145); fade >=14d / archive >=90d / online wins / reverts on activity. Add a core test with an injected clock for lastActiveAt (3 sources + floor), and a UI-module test for the thresholds and  [full: .full.txt]

Reversal is not 'at once' (acceptance 3). lastActiveAt lives in state.actorsList, refetched only on 60s TTL via ensureActors callers or when an unknown actor appears (zdarzenia-sse.js:123 refetches only if absent from cache). An archived actor that posts via API with no live session (handleOnline false) stays archived/faded in an open tab until reload. Refresh actors on a message event from a faded/archived actor, or bump lastActiveAt locally.

Query plan (seeded 10k messages/50 actors): 'SCAN messages USING INDEX idx_messages_actor' materialised per GET /api/actors call; 2.2 ms/call now, but linear in total messages (no per-actor scan, yet one full scan per call, and the index lacks ts so each row is a table lookup). Add INDEX messages(actor_id, ts) and use a correlated (SELECT MAX(ts) FROM messages WHERE actor_id=a.id) for 50 seeks.

Activity signal is weaker than the intent in the brief ('session/read'): sessions rows are deleted 7 days after death (presence.ts:138 MARTWA_SESJA_SEK), so a read-only agent that works daily through tokens but sends no messages has lastActiveAt reduced to created_at once its sessions are gone, and fades/archives after 14/90 days of real use. tokens.last_used_at (tokens.ts:126, throttled to 1 min) is the durable signal; include it in the MAX.

Leak check (acceptance 5): GET /api/actors (any authenticated viewer) now exposes the timestamp of each actor's latest message regardless of conversation visibility - MAX(ts) covers private channels, DMs and soft-deleted messages (no deleted_at filter, no membership filter). Content is not leaked, only timing; a DM sent at time T shows up as T to everybody. Consider excluding dm/private/deleted rows or coarsening to the day.
